purpose: Keep the tools page calm, local-first, and easy to scan on desktop and touch screens.

referenceHierarchy.use: Primary visual source of truth: editorial hierarchy, neutral canvas, restrained semantic accents.
Audit lens: explicit hierarchy, consistent tokens, anti-slop restraint, and a clear reason for every visual element.
Mobile reference only: health states should be legible, quiet when normal, and obvious when attention is needed.
Interaction reference: use transform and opacity for short feedback, and always honor reduced motion.
Component reference only: borrow Spotlight Card, Glare Hover, Shiny Text, and compact control composition patterns without adding a React dependency.
Motion reference only: borrow the restrained grid atmosphere, pointer-reactive lighting, category rail, and scroll reveal cadence without copying unrelated scenes.
Layout reference only: borrow the floating workspace shell, sidebar, KPI strip, dashboard content area, and progressive section hierarchy while keeping Fitness Ledger copy and data contracts.
Effect direction only: select bounded 3D/WebGL demos for the isolated Motion Lab; do not replace the archive workflow with a showcase landing page.
Implementation source for the Motion Lab head-and-bugs experiment: reuse the public BugRig, CCDIK, raycast cage, and instanced animation build with attribution.
Implementation source for the Motion Lab cursor ripple experiment: reuse the public Three.js/GLSL build and only adapt wrapper copy and palette.
Temporary full-body muscular GLB fallback for the Guardian Pose Deck; the pose controller is asset-agnostic and will accept an authorized Nick Walker GLB without a UI rewrite.
Open architecture reference for a full-body character that follows the cursor and triggers actions on click; adapted locally with the existing pet routing and reduced-motion boundary.
Interaction reference for right-click / long-press menu anatomy, collision-aware placement, dismissal, focus, and keyboard navigation; implemented locally in vanilla JS.
Implementation source for hierarchical 3D transforms on ordinary DOM elements; the existing HTML buttons remain the accessible interaction authority.
Pattern reference for interactive 3D panels, nested surfaces, depth, and button feedback; adapted to the project's vanilla HTML/CSS surface instead of replacing business controls with canvas text.
Implementation source for the small desktop companion's spring/inertia cursor following; the body and eyes are local project pixel sprites.

implementation.template: Collective OS dashboard anatomy adapted locally; no runtime dependency
implementation.reactBits: Spotlight Card and Glare Hover patterns adapted locally in vanilla CSS
implementation.css3dPanels: not mounted on the template adapter; semantic DOM controls remain the interaction authority
implementation.mousePet: local adapted MIT mouse-follower spring/inertia behavior with a borderless full-body Guardian pet using the five low-poly static-pose assets and pointer messages sent into its Three.js mesh
implementation.motion: Invisigrid Motion Lab-inspired grid atmosphere, pointer spotlight, and scroll reveal; bounded and reduced-motion safe
implementation.motionLab: Isolated route with Easy Bugs for head/IK surface movement, 3D Wave Grid for cursor ripples, and a small global Guardian Pet backed by five low-poly static-pose assets. The full-body Pose Deck remains asset QA only; the pilot has no archive API access.
implementation.upperField: Use the side whitespace for quiet, source-derived rails and a small route map; do not stretch the hero to fill it.
implementation.archiveField: Use the Collective OS sidebar, KPI strip, dashboard grid, border rhythm, status badges, route rows, and a restrained Wave Grid accent inside an existing module; keep the paper canvas quiet and do not add a detached 3D layer.
implementation.archiveCore: Export remains a separate one-off operation. Archive Health owns Sync and Data Check as two explicit action rows, while Movement Dictionary remains a separate reference entry. Sync keeps only state, route, action, verification, and progressive diagnostics.
implementation.globalPet: The global guardian is a borderless 58px transparent full-body Three.js pet using the same five low-poly static-pose assets as the isolated Pose Deck. Pointer follow is sent into the scene; pose switching remains available from the pet menu, wheel, keyboard, custom event, postMessage, and window.__fitnessLedgerGuardianPet.
implementation.dataPolicy: derive visual status from existing state; never invent health or sync data

constraints: Do not change Analysis Export or Movement Dictionary protocol semantics; Cloud Sync and Data Health protocols remain unchanged while their presentation is redesigned.
Do not add a second source of truth or copy formal data into the worktree.
Do not add remote runtime dependencies; the MIT-licensed Gentelella page anatomy is adapted locally and documented in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md.
The page title must name the utility surface; do not replace it with a campaign-style slogan.

Motion Lab is an explicit experimental route; Sync, Data Check, and Export never host WebGPU/canvas demos. Movement Dictionary may host only a read-only Easy Bugs reference preview with no archive API access.
Do not pair oversized display type with explanatory microcopy unless it clarifies a real action.
Use rounded pills only for real status or navigation; never as decorative labels.
Use the template's border, status, and action-row feedback; do not lift every card or add decorative 3D motion.
Decorative marks must explain the archive surface or its three routes; no invented status, badges, or visual filler.
The paper canvas and shared border rhythm must connect the panels without becoming a second content layer or changing semantic state.
Keep primary actions keyboard reachable with visible focus styles.
Keep the page usable at narrow widths and disable decorative motion for prefers-reduced-motion.
acceptance: Export and Archive Health remain the two primary operation surfaces; Sync and Data Check remain reachable through their current data-tools-panel hooks, and Movement Dictionary stays a separate reference entry.
Desktop reads as one maintenance desk with a clear primary action.
Mobile stacks the same content without horizontal overflow and preserves touch target size.
Visual motion is non-blocking and limited to short transform feedback on real controls.
The template adapter stays usable without a CSS3D or canvas layer on touch and reduced-motion contexts.
The original ghost remains available across all routes, and its context menu reaches the existing navigation routes without introducing a second router.
